source_text: However, empirical assessments reveal persistent consent deficiencies: in Eswatini, males aged 10-19 exhibited limited grasp of procedure risks post-counseling, with sessions disproportionately highlighting benefits while downplaying adverse events like infection or excessive skin removal, and misconceptions persisted that HIV testing was obligatory rather than optional. [125]
